text_en: England announced squad for T20 World Cup 2022 : Following Australia, England announced its squad for the T20 World Cup. By dropping explosive batter Jason Roy ( Jason Roy), the England Cricket Board made a major decision. Roy's form had not been anything special. Since Jofra Archer has still not recovered fitness, he will miss yet another World Cup. Alex Hales is also not part of the 15-member squad. Both of them are set to return after March. Jonny Bairstow and Jos Buttler will open the batting. Jofra Archer did not play in the 2021 World Cup either; he is expected to make a comeback at the 2023 ODI World Cup. Jos Buttler will tour Pakistan despite being injured, but he will not play the first few matches there. - Amruta Kadam When we plan a trip, very few people will deliberately consider going to Odisha. Since it has still not become very prominent on the tourist map, one may even wonder what exactly there is to see here. But this state, located on India's eastern coast, is famous for its temples. For its distinctive music and dance styles. And yes, for its seafood too. Odisha's capital Bhubaneswar is known as the 'Temple Capital' for exactly this reason. It is said that between the 7th and 12th centuries, this city had as many as 7000 temples. Today, however, only as many temples remain as can be counted on one's fingers. Experts believe the Parasuramesvara Temple is the oldest temple in Bhubaneswar. This temple was built in 650 CE. The spire of this temple is shaped like a honeycomb. In front of the temple is a vast courtyard. Eight planets are carved on the entrance. Later, a ninth planet was added to this series. Along with images of gods and goddesses, the walls here also bear carvings of scenes from scriptures and of the temple's daily religious rituals. The design of this temple is in the Kalinga architectural style. A feature of the temples here is that these temples, built in different periods, show us different architectural styles. Even if you are not an expert in history or architecture, the architecture of these temples will captivate you. Another well-known temple in Bhubaneswar is the Kotitirtheswara Temple. It is a temple to Harihara. This is the largest temple in Bhubaneswar. In fact, it is a complex of temples. The spire of the main temple is as high as 55 metres. This alone gives an idea of the grandeur of the temples here. The temple we see today dates from the 11th century. But construction of the original temple began in the 6th century. According to some Sanskrit texts, it began in the 7th century. This temple in Kalinga style is a rich cultural heritage. Alongside the temples, the sacred name associated here is that of Bindusagar Lake. Many legends are linked to this lake. To give thirsty Parvati water to drink, Shiva struck the ground with his trident, and a spring emerged there. It was from this spring that Bindusagar Lake was formed. Close to this spring stands the Ananta Vasudeva Temple. This temple of Lord Vishnu was built in the 13th century by Queen Chandrika of the Ganga dynasty. The Marathas carried out the restoration of this temple. Although the temple is dedicated to Vishnu, its architecture is largely similar to the Lingaraja Temple. Potato or any other foreign vegetable is not used in this prasad, which is cooked in clay pots. Moreover, vegetables that do not grow in a given season are also not used in the prasad here. So consider how difficult it is to prepare the prasad here. It is not only the Ananta Vasudeva Temple; this practice is followed in many temples across Odisha. Places associated not only with Hinduism but also with Jainism are found here. The Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves here are famous. These caves, in Jain architectural style, are very ancient examples. These are only the temples of Bhubaneswar. Considering Odisha as a whole, the Jagannath Temple in Puri and the Konark Sun Temple, declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site, are also major tourist attractions. Overall, if your trip to Odisha or Bhubaneswar is not merely religious tourism, it will also be an attempt to understand a rich historical and cultural heritage. So when you plan your next trip, be sure to consider Odisha.

New Delhi: The Uddhav Thackeray and Eknath Shinde factions are making every effort to gain control of the Shiv Sena. In the midst of this, the Election Commission has, for the time being, allotted the Shinde and Thackeray factions a party name and election symbol each. Accordingly, on Monday the Thackeray faction was given the torch (mashal) symbol. The Shinde faction, meanwhile, was asked for three new symbol options. Reports say the Shinde faction's symbol has now been finalised. The Thackeray faction had been granted the blazing torch as its election symbol. Sources told ABP Majha that the Election Commission would today allot the Shinde faction the blazing sun symbol. It was also said that this symbol would be announced shortly. The options sent included the blazing sun, shield and sword, and the peepal tree. The Shinde faction had also claimed these very symbols. As a result, they did not get either of these symbols. The third symbol was the blazing torch. This symbol had earlier been allotted to another party, the Samata Party. But since that party no longer exists, the symbol has now returned to the free pool and has been given to the Thackeray faction. However, this symbol is valid only for the Andheri East by-election. The Election Commission stated in its order that a final decision on this would be taken after the adjudication now underway before the Commission. The rising sun symbol was rejected because it belongs to the DMK in Tamil Nadu. Because of this, the Commission had rejected all three symbols proposed by the Shinde faction. Now, instead of the rising sun, the risen sun will be given to the Shinde faction. The Shinde faction had given first preference to the name Shiv Sena (Balasaheb Thackeray), and second preference to Balasahebanchi Shiv Sena. The Uddhav Thackeray faction had given first preference to Shiv Sena (Balasaheb Thackeray). Since both factions claimed the same name, the Election Commission rejected this claim, and the second-preference name was Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray).

As every year, this year too the online admission process for Class 11 has been started before the Class 10 results are published, and its tentative schedule has been announced. With the aim that students be admitted based on the marks they obtained in Class 10 and their preference order, the Education Department has been running the online admission process since the 2017-18 academic year. This year too, Class 11 admissions in schools and junior colleges in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, the Pune and Pimpri Chinchwad municipal areas, and the Nashik, Aurangabad, Amravati and Nagpur municipal corporation areas will be given online. Admissions to the remaining junior colleges will be made at the college level. All divisional deputy directors of education offices should provide students and parents with the necessary guidance on this. The state Director of Secondary Education, Mahesh Palkar, has also instructed that the necessary admission planning and action plan be prepared. The Class 11 admission process will actually begin in the coming month of May. In it, 10 to 15 days will be given for the first round, and 7 to 9 days each for the second and third rounds. After that, a special round and, for the remaining students, admissions will be given using a waiting-list method instead of a first-come, first-served priority round.

Nagpur: After the swearing-in of the state cabinet, there was a reshuffle within the BJP in the state. Chandrashekhar Bawankule has been appointed state president of the BJP, while Ashish Shelar has been named president of the Mumbai BJP. Against the backdrop of Bawankule becoming state BJP president, a felicitation event in his honour was held in Nagpur today. Union Minister Nitin Gadkari, Deputy Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and other important BJP leaders attended the event. Everyone recounted Bawankule's life journey so far and congratulated him. But the speech by Union Minister Nitin Gadkari drew the most attention. Gadkari, in his characteristic style, delivered a storm of witty jabs. You know well what happens to whoever becomes state president. I am not wishing you well for the chief minister's post, mind you; otherwise, the media will attribute to me things I never said. Fadnavis must be the chief minister, but after he goes to the Centre, Bawankule, we may consider you," Nitin Gadkari said with a sly smile, and the hall erupted in laughter. BJP workers also began loud slogan-shouting in support of Bawankule. He will also get scope to showcase his abilities. This is a party of workers. It is not a party of father-son or mother-son. An ordinary man who drove an auto-rickshaw has today become the state president of Maharashtra, through his ability and work. This is a distinctive feature of the BJP. Honouring a worker is a matter of joy for me, Devendra Fadnavis and all workers," Nitin Gadkari said. Because they know these questions. Another important point is that our party needs to increase its strength in the coming period. Because if any party has the strength to change Maharashtra's future, that strength lies only in the BJP. So, under Devendra-ji's leadership, governance work will certainly get done. But the organisation must also be equally strong. We have to expand the party through both strengths," Nitin Gadkari also said.
